old: Modals like *kell* (must / have to), *lehet* (can / may / is possible), and *muszáj* (compulsory / must) take a dative subject (*-nak / -nek*) and an infinitive.
new: You know *kell* and *muszáj* (A1, Unit 24), *lehet* (A1, Unit 30) and inflected infinitives (A2, Unit 21). In a general statement the infinitive stays plain: *Sok vizet kell inni.* When a person is named, the dative (*-nak / -nek*) goes on the person and the infinitive takes a personal ending: *Az embernek innia kell.*
why: Rule is false for the examples (no dative subject in either) and presents kell/lehet/muszáj and inflected infinitives as new (A1 Unit 24/30, A2 Unit 21).

old: *Szabad* indicates permission ('is allowed'), while *tilos* or *nem szabad* indicates strict prohibition ('forbidden / not permitted'). Both govern the infinitive.
new: You know *szabad* and *tilos* from A2 (Unit 23): *szabad* gives permission ('is allowed'), *tilos* or *nem szabad* forbids ('not permitted'), and both go with the infinitive. Here they appear on health signs and warnings.
why: Screen presents szabad/tilos as new (szabad-infinitive is A2 Unit 23).
